character_master:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: finished character-development hero render for Mustache Massacre.
Input images: image 1 is the actual detailed Don Espino 3D model and the primary identity reference; image 2 is the user's original FBX render and the authoritative style reference. The original render has overlapping mirrored face pieces; use the repaired bilateral face in image 1.
Primary request: produce a much more polished, richly detailed but faithful render of THIS SAME character, full body in a poised gunslinger stance with his silver six-shot revolver held low in his right hand. His opposite hand rests by the belt. A simple charcoal warm-gray studio background and grounding shadow.
IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the tall green cylindrical cactus torso with subtle vertical ribs, unusually thin green arms and green shins, small tan cowboy boots, orange-brown SHORTS and simple leather belt with rectangular brass buckle, oversized brown cowboy hat with the very tall asymmetric double-lobed split crown and wide soft brim, dark leather hatband with a gold five-point sheriff star. Preserve the enormous two-lobed brown moustache sweeping DOWN to pointed tips, heavy blocky brown eyebrows, small black eyes, small white cigarette, the gray belt radio with antenna and orange buttons and the red-and-cream unlabelled packet. The hat and torso proportions must match the reference. No poncho, coat, bandolier, gloves, human skin or chibi body.
Detail improvement: waxy botanical cactus skin with restrained irregular areoles and short ivory spines; subtle organic vertical ridges; moustache groomed as broad sculpted clumps with fine directional grooves, not individual realistic hair; felt fibers and compressed hat edges, clean saddle stitching seated exactly on the hatband; warm worn leather boots with seams, toe decoration and subtle dust; woven shorts with restrained seams and folds; aged brass star and buckle; engraved steel revolver frame, distinct six-chamber cylinder, wood-grain grip. Hand must visibly grip the revolver correctly.
Expression: stern, annoyed, dead-serious little gunslinger, brows angled down toward the center, no smile. Pose gives life to the model while keeping its awkward thin-limbed identity.
Style/medium: high-quality stylized 3D game character render, rounded hand-sculpted forms, clean broad shapes, artful material separation. Remain close to the handmade cartoon style in the FBX rather than cinematic photorealism.
Composition: portrait, single large full-body character, complete hat and boots visible, subtle three-quarter front view, entire character sharply legible. Soft warm key and restrained cool rim light, readable brown moustache against green skin. No text, labels, UI, logo, watermark, extra weapons or extra limbs.

scenes.name: 02_ricochet_rodeo
scenes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: finished combat visual-development render for Mustache Massacre.
Reference roles: image 1 is the polished Don Espino identity master; image 2 is the actual detailed 3D model and authoritative silhouette. Preserve the same character and clothing across the set.
Identity lock: tall narrow green cylindrical cactus torso, subtle vertical ribs, thin green arms and shins, small tan boots, ochre-orange SHORTS and belt with rectangular brass buckle, giant brown hat with a very tall asymmetric double-lobed split crown, dark hatband and gold sheriff star, heavy brown brows, small black eyes, huge thick two-lobed brown moustache with downward-swept pointed ends, small cigarette, gray belt radio with antenna and colored buttons, red-and-cream unlabelled packet. Keep his thin limbs, long body, high-crowned hat and handmade cartoon proportions. No poncho, coat, bandolier, gloves or human anatomy. Standard weapon is one silver six-shot revolver with dark wood grip.
Style: premium stylized 3D game render, broad smooth sculpted shapes, crisp silhouette, tactile but restrained felt, canvas, worn leather, waxy cactus skin, sparse ivory spines and directional moustache grooves. Charming absurd enemies and exaggerated action with a stern unsmiling hero. Do not turn into photorealism, gritty illustration or a squat chibi cactus.
Composition: landscape widescreen single scene, dynamic three-quarter isometric action camera low enough to read the face; Don Espino is large in foreground at least 40% of image height; show complete hat and both boots. Clear spatial separation between player, targets and effects, clean readable silhouette. Match the model's face and clothing in every scene. No captions, text, logo, watermark, HUD or damage numbers. No gore. No extra limbs or detached hands; revolver sits properly in his gripping hand.
Scene: The Crispy Badlands, a dusty cracked saloon street, collapsed wooden porch, red sandstone rocks, a few fuel drums, warm late-afternoon sun. Keep architecture secondary and the horizon uncluttered.
Attack: Ricochet Rodeo with the fan-the-hammer upgrade. Don Espino slides sideways into a braced firing stance, body leaning against recoil, right hand aims his single revolver, left palm fans the hammer. An oversized sharp gold muzzle flash and ONE clearly connected angular golden ricochet trail bounce through three well-separated ridiculous moustachioed enemies: a hostile tumbleweed, a muscular pigeon and an angry vegetable. Each bounce has a small distinct spark and exaggerated cartoon hit reaction. The path must visibly change direction AT the struck targets. Three or four kicked-up dust clumps behind his boots show movement.
Effect hierarchy: Don's face, hat and revolver remain fully readable; thin golden bullet lines carry the eye across the scene. Dust is restrained. A little squash-and-stretch in the lean, the hat and moustache follow the motion. Color: warm sand and burnt orange, green cactus focal point, gold bullet accents.
Attack expression: inner brow tips pulled DOWN toward the nose and outer ends raised in a fierce V, eyes narrowed with resolve; expressive anger rather than sad or pleading eyebrows. Keep the distinctive blocky brows.
